newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan five-year bonds average yield 8.54 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jordan five-year bonds average yield 8.54 percent.

text.p: Jordan's Central Bank announced on Tuesday it had issued treasury bonds worth 12 million dinars ($16.9 million) with an average yield of 8.54 percent in its first competitive bills auction.
They were 80 percent oversubscribed, the bank said.
The bonds, sold in blocs of 1,000 dinars each, are traded instruments with their gains exempt from tax. The bank said yields accepted varied from 8.47 percent to 8.70 percent.
Jordan's Central Bank has introduced competitive bidding for bills and certificates of deposits (CDs), the main government debt instrument, as part of moves towards liberalising its money markets.
The last bonds to be issued were seven-year bills. They were offered last September at a uniform rate of 9.25 percent.
